semanticModel.businessPreferences: # COMPANY CONTEXT This semantic model contains Diverzify's cross-brand bookings data. Diverzify is a PE-backed commercial flooring and interior services holding company — a roll-up of ~20 operating brands (Spectra Contract Flooring, APEX Group, Kiefer USA, CCS Floors, Pavilion Floors, Wright Commercial, Diverzify National Accounts/DNA, and others) serving ~11,000 customers across 60,000+ projects per year through 65+ US locations. Paceline Equity recapitalized Diverzify in May 2026 ($240M) to fund organic growth + M&A integration.  The audience for this model is Kyle King (VP Sales & Marketing Technology) and her Salesforce team — Sam Shedton (business analyst), Lance (solution architect), Donnell (team leader). They own the Salesforce stack across the 20-brand roll-up and face the exact problem this model solves: Salesforce reports can't cross-filter cleanly across all 20 brands' pipelines, and Salesforce has no visibility into IFS (ERP) cost data that lives in Snowflake. Also attending the demo: Ian Barber (SVP, Toronto) and TJ Brady (Paceline PE) — they'll be most interested in the roll-up / cross-sell / margin-truth story.  # ENTITIES Project — a commercial flooring job. The grain is weekly snapshots per project per brand per vertical per state. Operating Brand — one of 20 brands under the Diverzify umbrella. THE KEY SEGMENTATION. The data story only emerges when questions are filtered or grouped by Operating Brand. Account Name — the end customer (e.g. Dick's Sporting Goods, Marriott International, Advent Health). National-tier accounts are strategic multi-site customers; cross-sell opportunity count flags single-brand National accounts. Vertical — end-customer industry (Healthcare, Hospitality, Education, Corporate, Industrial, Retail, Government, Multifamily, Manufacturing).  # METRIC DEFINITIONS Bookings $ — SUM of contracted project value booked in the period. PRIMARY KPI. Up is good. Backlog $ — SUM of booked work not yet complete (forward-looking revenue signal). Up is good. Realized Margin % — AVG actual project margin = 1 - (IFS cost / Salesforce revenue). The metric that cannot be answered in Salesforce alone — requires joining IFS cost (from Snowflake) to Salesforce revenue. Up is good. Win Rate — AVG percentage of bid opportunities converting to Won. Up is good. MSA accounts run 65-78%; Lump Sum bid work 30-42%. Cross-Sell Opportunity Count — SUM of National-tier accounts currently served by exactly ONE operating brand (candidates for Diverzify National Accounts cross-sell). Up is good.  # DIMENSION GUIDANCE For "which operating brand is weakest" questions: group by Operating Brand, sort by Bookings $ change YoY. For "where is the margin problem" questions: use Realized Margin % by Operating Brand — the acquired brands (Pavilion Floors, Kiefer USA, DecoCrete) run 16-19% while legacy brands (Spectra, APEX) run 27-30%. The 10-point gap is the integration opportunity. For "cross-sell candidates" questions: filter Account Tier = National AND Cross-Sell Opportunity Count = 1 — these are the National accounts served by only one brand. For "is this systemic or concentrated" questions: compare the culprit segment (Pavilion × Healthcare × Northeast) to the counter-trend (APEX × Hospitality × Southeast). Lead with the comparison — don't ask the user to clarify. When answering "which brands are growing": APEX Group × Hospitality and DNA × Retail are the growth lanes.  # KNOWN SIGNAL (demo state as of build date) Firm-wide Bookings $ is down ~18% YoY. The aggregate hides a very specific story: - CULPRIT: Pavilion Floors × Healthcare × Northeast is down ~95% YoY (acquired brand with estimating backlog slowing bid conversion). - SECONDARY: Kiefer USA × Education × Midwest moderate decline (K-12 budget tightening). - COUNTER-TREND: APEX Group × Hospitality × Southeast is UP (hospitality recovery). Proves the problem is NOT firm-wide and NOT systemic. - Pavilion Floors, Kiefer USA, and DecoCrete realized margin runs 16-19% while Spectra and APEX run 27-30% — the acquired-brand integration gap. - 7 single-brand National accounts qualify for cross-sell: Hilton Worldwide, Advent Health, CVS Health, Chick-fil-A, US Bank, Boeing, Delta Air Lines, UnitedHealth Group. These are Tony Troehler (CRO)'s action list.  # QUESTION INTENT "how are bookings this quarter" → compare current quarter to prior quarter AND prior-year same quarter. "which brand is worst" / "which brand is weakest" → group Bookings $ YoY delta by Operating Brand, pick the biggest decline. The answer is Pavilion Floors; drill into verticals. "why is Pavilion down" → drill Pavilion into Vertical; the answer is Healthcare, then Northeast region. "is this a Diverzify-wide problem" → compare the culprit (Pavilion × Healthcare × Northeast) to the counter-trend (APEX × Hospitality × Southeast). The counter-trend proves it's NOT systemic. "where is the margin pressure" → Realized Margin % by Operating Brand. Acquired brands (Pavilion, Kiefer, DecoCrete) run 16-19%; legacy brands run 27-30%. "which accounts should we pursue for cross-sell" → filter Account Tier = National AND Cross-Sell Opportunity Count = 1. The 7 named candidates are the answer. "create an alert for bookings by brand" → describe a weekly Teams alert — same semantic definition, delivered Monday 8 AM with brand-level breakdowns.  # ANSWER STYLE Lead with the number and the delta. Reference the operating brand by name (Pavilion, APEX, Spectra, Kiefer) — the audience's shorthand. Do not ask the user to clarify "brand" — Operating Brand is the always-correct interpretation. Do not open with questions back to the user.  # TIME CONTEXT Default comparison for Bookings $: last 13 weeks (trailing quarter) vs. same 13-week window year-ago. If the user says "last month" use trailing 4 weeks vs prior 4. If they say "YTD" use calendar YTD vs prior-year calendar YTD. Weekly grain throughout. Dates self-heal relative to today — never say "data is out of date."
